topics.title: Sensory processing differences in autism: senses, profiles and theories
topics.scope: The eight senses (incl. interoception, proprioception, vestibular), hyper- vs hyposensitivity, sensory profiles and Dunn's model, Irlen syndrome, gravitational insecurity, and brain-level theories (predictive coding, habituation, disrupted connectivity) of autistic sensory sensitivity.

topics.title: Sensory regulation, stimming and sensory safety plans
topics.scope: Practical self-regulation of the sensory system: functions of stimming, calming techniques (deep pressure, breathing, sound, light, smell, visuals), the five-part sensory safety plan, holiday overload checks, tolerating discomfort, and useful sensory tools.

topics.title: Meltdowns and shutdowns: triggers, differences and recovery
topics.scope: What causes meltdowns and shutdowns, how outward loss of control differs from inward withdrawal, coping strategies (triggers, safe space, routine) and what to do after a meltdown, including how close people can help.

topics.title: Autistic and ADHD burnout, boom-or-bust and pacing
topics.scope: Autistic/neurodivergent burnout (causes, symptoms, recovery), the boom-or-bust cycle and its vulnerability factors, pacing systems (energy accounting, spoon theory, traffic light), workload norms and survey data on neurodivergent people's work resilience.

topics.title: Pathological demand avoidance (PDA) and the PANDA approach
topics.scope: The PDA profile as anxiety-driven avoidance of demands, its escalation from hidden coping to panic and meltdown, debate over whether it is a separate diagnosis, and the PANDA skill for living and communicating with demand avoidance.

topics.title: Masking and camouflaging: forms, costs and measurement
topics.scope: What masking is (hypervigilance, controlled self-expression, silence and shyness), how ableism and rejection sensitivity drive it, its costs (overcontrol, burnout, loss of self), the CAT-Q questionnaire with scoring, how autistic identity forms, and why girls and women with ADHD and autism are underdiagnosed.

topics.title: Autistic communication, empathy and friendship
topics.scope: Typical autistic communication traits (literalness, infodumping, small talk), the double empathy problem and its replication, mentalizing, empathy survey results, object personification, friendship and loneliness research, autistic culture and representation, and when to apologize.

topics.title: Executive function, autistic inertia, time perception and object permanence
topics.scope: Executive dysfunction in autism and ADHD, types and mechanisms of attention, sluggish cognitive tempo, ADHD time perception, autistic inertia with helpers like body doubling, object permanence in relationships and conflicts, and why rest alone does not fix self-organisation.

topics.title: Hyperfocus, special interests and monotropism
topics.scope: Special interests and their benefits, hyperfocus versus flow in ADHD and autism, monotropism theory, research measuring hyperfocus in autistic teens, and how autistic adults tell special interests and stims apart from OCD.

topics.title: Boredom, boring tasks and mindfulness for ADHD
topics.scope: Why boredom is more frequent and painful in ADHD/ASD (apathetic vs agitated), how to make boring tasks bearable, and the evidence for and adaptations of mindfulness practice for ADHD attention.

topics.title: Autism traits beyond the stereotypes: lesser-known features and aphantasia
topics.scope: Core ICD-11 criteria and lesser-known autism features (non-communication behaviors, echopraxia, clumsiness, selective mutism, self-reported traits), the broader autism phenotype, and aphantasia and its link to autism.

topics.title: AuDHD, differential diagnosis and self-report questionnaires
topics.scope: Co-occurring autism and ADHD, autism vs bipolar disorder, ADHD vs antisocial personality, the HiTOP dimensional view, childhood ADHD and parent training, ADHD in high-IQ people, positive ADHD traits, underdiagnosis of ADHD and autism in women, and what self-report questionnaires (RAADS, MQ, ABM, CAT-Q, NIAS) can and cannot tell.

topics.title: Research on autism and ADHD: brain, genetics, diagnosis trends and reading
topics.scope: Study summaries on the amygdala in autism, autism gene regulatory networks, early vs late diagnosis trajectories, rising diagnosis rates without an 'epidemic', online discourse on ADHD and autism, plus reviews of clinical and autistic-authored books.

topics.title: Alexithymia and interoception in autism
topics.scope: The alexithymia hypothesis of autism, how alexithymia rather than autism explains interoception differences, a behaviorist view, and a timed spoken exercise for clarifying what you feel and why.

domains.domain: Therapy and coping skills for neurodivergent adults

topics.title: DBT for autistic adults: rationale, adaptations and evidence
topics.scope: Why DBT rather than CBT suits autistic clients, prevalence of emotion dysregulation, ASD-specific adaptations (masking vs skills, alexithymia, sensory profile), conference reports and the Strasbourg RCT showing reduced dysregulation via alexithymia.

topics.title: Distress tolerance and self-care skills for neurodivergent people
topics.scope: DBT crisis skills (distraction acronym, STOP) for surviving peak emotions and interrupting harmful coping, self-care when feeling bad, and self-care cards for neurodivergent people (self-acceptance, support team, structure, technology).

topics.title: Anxiety, PTSD and OCD in autistic people
topics.scope: Prevalence and causes of anxiety, social anxiety and PTSD in autism, how masking feeds them, adapted treatment and self-help, OCD self-observation with Y-BOCS, and distinguishing OCD from special interests and stims.

domains.domain: Physical health and the neurodivergent body

topics.title: Physical comorbidities, sleep and hormones in autism and ADHD
topics.scope: Research-linked physical traits (GI issues, hypermobility/EDS, POTS, fibromyalgia), sleep disorders and melatonin for delayed sleep phase in ADHD, evidence on supplements for autism, and ADHD in perimenopause.
